Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## Quick answer Yes – the **MapLibre style-spec CLI** can validate a style JSON for you. ```bash # 1️⃣ Install the validator (dev-dependency is fine) npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec # 2️⃣ Run it on your file npx gl-style-validate path/to/your-style.json ``` If the file is compatible you’ll see something like: ``` ✔ style is valid (0 errors, 0 warnings) ``` If there are problems the tool prints each error/warning with a line number and a short description, so you can fix them before you ship. Below is a full walk-through, plus tips for CI, common pitfalls, and what to do after the validator tells you the style is “valid”. --- ## 1️⃣ Install the CLI | Option | Command | When to use | |--------|---------|-------------| | **npm (recommended)** | `npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` | You already have a Node project (most front-end builds do). | | **yarn** | `yarn add -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` | You use Yarn. | | **pnpm** | `pnpm add -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` | You use pnpm. | | **global (quick test)** | `npm i -g @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` | You just want a one-off check without adding a dependency. | > **Why a dev-dependency?** > The validator is only needed at build / CI time, not in the production bundle, so keeping it in `devDependencies` keeps your production bundle lean. --- ## 2️⃣ Run the validator ```bash # Basic usage npx gl-style-validate ./style.json # Verbose output (shows every warning & error with JSON-pointer) npx gl-style-validate ./style.json --verbose # Only warnings (ignore errors – not recommended for CI) npx gl-style-validate ./style.json --warnings # Output as JSON (handy for CI scripts) npx gl-style-validate ./style.json --format json ``` ### Example output (invalid style) ``` ✖ 2 errors, 1 warning Error /sources/openstreetmap/type must be one of ["vector","raster","geojson","image","video"] Error /layers/0/source-layer must be a non-empty string Warning /layers/5/paint/line-color unknown property "line-color" ``` Each line tells you: * **JSON-pointer** – where in the file the problem lives (`/sources/...`, `/layers/...`). * **Message** – what the spec expects. * **Severity** – `Error` (fails validation) or `Warning` (still loads but may not behave as you expect). Fix the issues, then re-run the command until you get a clean “✔ style is valid”. --- ## 3️⃣ What the validator actually checks | Category | What it validates | Why it matters for MapLibre | |----------|-------------------|-----------------------------| | **Top-level keys** | `version`, `sources`, `layers`, `sprite`, `glyphs`, `metadata`, `center`, `zoom`, `bearing`, `pitch`, `sky` (if present) | MapLibre follows the **MapLibre Style Specification** (a fork of the Mapbox spec). Missing or miss-spelled keys cause the map to refuse to load. | | **Source definitions** | `type` (`vector`, `raster`, `geojson`, `image`, `video`), `url`/`tiles`, `minzoom`/`maxzoom`, `attribution` | MapLibre does **not** understand `mapbox://` URLs. The validator will flag any `type: "vector"` source that still points at `mapbox://…`. | | **Layer definitions** | `id`, `type`, `source`, `source-layer` (for vector sources), `paint`, `layout`, `filter` | If you exported a Mapbox Studio style, the `source-layer` names often need to be changed to match the new tile source (e.g., `road` → `roads`). | | **Sprite & glyph URLs** | Must be absolute HTTP(S) URLs or relative to the style file | MapLibre will try to fetch them; a missing sprite leads to blank icons. | | **Expressions & paint properties** | Valid syntax, correct value types, supported property names for the target MapLibre version | Some Mapbox-only properties (e.g., `fill-extrusion-pattern`) are not yet supported in MapLibre v6 – they appear as errors. | | **Experimental features** | `sky`, `terrain`, `projection` (globe) – only if the MapLibre version you run supports them | If you use `setFog` in Mapbox, you’ll need to replace it with a `sky` object; the validator will flag the old `fog` key. | > **Tip:** The validator uses the **latest released spec** (v6.x at the time of writing). If you are running an older MapLibre version (e.g., v5), you can pass `--spec-version 5` to validate against that version. ```bash npx gl-style-validate ./style.json --spec-version 5 ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Integrating the check into CI / npm scripts Add a script to your `package.json`: ```json { "scripts": { "style:check": "gl-style-validate ./src/style.json", "style:check:ci": "gl-style-validate ./src/style.json --format json > style-report.json" } } ``` Then in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, etc.: ```yaml - name: Validate MapLibre style run: npm run style:check ``` If the command exits with a non-zero status (any error), the CI job fails – preventing a broken style from reaching production. --- ## 5️⃣ Common “gotchas” after a successful validation Even when the validator says *“valid”*, you may still see blank tiles or missing icons. Those are usually **runtime data problems**, not spec problems. | Symptom | Likely cause | How to verify | |---------|--------------|---------------| | No basemap tiles appear | Source URL points to a Mapbox `mapbox://` endpoint or to a private tile server that requires a token you didn’t supply. | Open the URL in a browser (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`). | | Icons are missing | `sprite` URL is wrong, or the sprite sheet does not contain the requested icon name. | Open the sprite JSON (`.../sprite.json`) and look for the icon name. | | Text looks garbled or missing | `glyphs` URL is missing or points to a non-existent font stack. | Load a glyph URL directly (`.../fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). | | 3-D terrain is flat | `terrain` source missing or `terrain` property not added to the style. | Verify the style has a `terrain` object and that the source is a raster-DEM or MVT-DEM source. | | `sky` appears black | You used the old `fog` object; MapLibre expects a `sky` object. | Replace `fog` with `sky` (see the table in the skill). | If you encounter any of these, the validator will **not** flag them because they are not spec errors – they are data-availability issues. --- ## 6️⃣ Editing a Mapbox-exported style for MapLibre 1. **Export the JSON** from Mapbox Studio (or via the Styles API). 2. **Search-replace** all `mapbox://` URLs: * `sources..url` → your new vector tile endpoint (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`). * `sprite` → a publicly reachable sprite sheet (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/liberty`). * `glyphs` → a glyph server (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). 3. **Adjust source-layer names** if the new tile source uses different layer IDs. *OpenFreeMap* uses `road`, `building`, `water`, etc.; Mapbox Studio may have `road_major`, `building` etc. Use the **TileJSON** of your source (`/tiles.json`) to see the exact `source-layer` names. 4. **Remove Mapbox-only keys** (`metadata.mapbox:...`, `fog`, `light` with Mapbox-only properties). 5. **Add a `sky` object** if you want atmosphere (optional). 6. **Run the validator** (`gl-style-validate`). Fix any errors it reports. 7. **Test in a browser** with a simple MapLibre page (see the “Minimal example” below). --- ## 7️⃣ Minimal MapLibre page to sanity-check the style ```html MapLibre style test
``` Open this file in a browser (or serve it with `npx serve .`) – if the map loads and you see the basemap, your style is good to go. --- ## 8️⃣ Full checklist for a safe deployment | ✅ | Step | |---|------| | 1 | Export style JSON from Mapbox Studio (or API). | | 2 | Replace **all** `mapbox://` URLs with your own tile, sprite, and glyph endpoints. | | 3 | Update `source-layer` names to match the new source (check the source’s TileJSON). | | 4 | Remove Mapbox-only keys (`fog`, `metadata.mapbox:*`, etc.). | | 5 | (Optional) Add a `sky` object if you want atmosphere. | | 6 | Install `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` (`npm i -D …`). | | 7 | Run `npx gl-style-validate ./style.json`. Fix any errors. | | 8 | Run the minimal MapLibre page locally to confirm tiles, sprites, and glyphs load. | | 9 | Add `npm run style:check` to your CI pipeline. | |10| Deploy – the map should render without the “style validation failed” console error. | --- ## 9️⃣ Alternative / supplemental tools | Tool | What it does | How to use | |------|--------------|------------| | **Maputnik** (web UI) | Visual editor + live validation against the spec. | Open `https://maputnik.github.io/`, load your JSON, fix errors interactively. | | **maplibre-gl-js-style-lint** (eslint plugin) | Lints style JSON as part of a JavaScript/TypeScript build. | `npm i -D maplibre-gl-js-style-lint` → add to your ESLint config. | | **@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec (Node API)** | Programmatic validation (useful for custom scripts). | ```js const {validate} = require('@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec'); const result = validate(styleObj); console.log(result.errors); ``` | | **CI integrations** | Some CI providers have pre-built actions (e.g., `maplibre/style-validator-action`). | Search the GitHub Marketplace for “MapLibre style validator”. | --- ## 10️⃣ TL;DR – One-liner for most projects ```bash npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec && npx gl-style-validate ./my-style.json ``` If you get “✔ style is valid”, you’re ready to point your MapLibre map at that JSON. If you see errors, the output tells you exactly which property needs fixing. --- ### Need more help? * **Missing a tile source?** Check the **awesome-maplibre** list for free vector tile providers (OpenFreeMap, OpenStreetMap Vector Tiles, MapTiler, etc.). * **Custom sprites or fonts?** See the **MapLibre Style Spec → Sprite & Glyphs** section for the exact URL patterns. * **Running into a Mapbox-only property?** Search the spec for the property name; if it’s not listed, you’ll need to drop or replace it

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-start “plug-and-play” way to get a **MapLibre map working without any API key**. It shows three ready-made, public style URLs you can drop into the `style` option, explains why they work, and gives a minimal example you can copy-paste into a sandbox (CodePen, StackBlitz, local `index.html`, etc.). --- ## 1️⃣ Pick a free, key-less style | Option | What it is | URL you can use in `new maplibregl.Map({ style: … })` | Why it works for testing | |--------|------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------| | **MapLibre demo style** (vector) | Official MapLibre demo that uses OpenStreetMap vector tiles hosted on `demotiles.maplibre.org`. | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` | No token, fully vector, includes sprites & glyphs, works out-of-the-box. | | **OpenFreeMap “liberty” style** (vector) | Community-run OSM-derived style, same format as Mapbox styles (`mapbox://`-like JSON) but hosted on a public URL. | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | Great if you want a style that looks like a Mapbox “streets” theme. | | **Raster OSM tiles + simple style** | If you only need a quick raster basemap, you can use the classic OSM raster tiles and a tiny style that points to them. | `https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json` (vector) **or** a custom style that references `https://{a-c}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Raster tiles are public; the Carto “positron” style is vector but also key-less. | > **Tip:** The MapLibre demo style (`demotiles.maplibre.org`) is the most “plug-and-play” because it already bundles a sprite sheet, glyphs, and a complete vector style. Use it first to verify that the library itself is working; then swap in your own style (OpenFreeMap, your own hosted style, or a self-generated PMTiles style) when you’re ready. --- ## 2️⃣ Minimal HTML / JavaScript example ```html MapLibre – key-less test map
``` **What this does** 1. Loads the **ES-module** build of MapLibre (v6+). 2. Points the map at a **public style JSON** that already knows where to fetch vector tiles, sprites, and glyphs. 3. No `maplibregl.accessToken` line – it’s not needed. Open the file in a browser (or paste the whole snippet into a CodePen/StackBlitz) and you should see a fully functional map. --- ## 3️⃣ If you want to use *your own* style JSON 1. **Export the style** you built in Mapbox Studio (or in Maputnik). 2. **Replace every `mapbox://` source URL** with a URL that points to a tile service you control or a public one. * Example conversion: ```json // Mapbox-style source (won’t work in MapLibre) { "type": "vector", "url": "mapbox://tileset-id" } ``` → change to a public vector tile endpoint, e.g.: ```json { "type": "vector", "tiles": ["https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"], "minzoom": 0, "maxzoom": 14 } ``` 3. **Update sprite & glyph URLs** if they still point at `api.mapbox.com`. * Sprite: `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/sprite` (or any URL that serves `sprite.png` + `sprite.json`). * Glyphs: `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf` (or use the default MapLibre glyphs at `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/font/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). 4. **Validate** the edited JSON with the MapLibre style spec CLI (optional but helpful): ```bash npx @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec validate path/to/your-style.json ``` 5. **Serve the JSON** (static file on your web server, GitHub Pages, Netlify, etc.) and point `style:` to that URL. --- ## 4️⃣ Quick list of other free vector-tile providers (no key) | Provider | Tile URL pattern | Notes | |----------|------------------|-------| | **OpenStreetMap Vector Tiles (OpenMapTiles)** | `https://{a-c}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf` (some community mirrors) | Not officially hosted by OSM; look for “openmaptiles.org” mirrors. | | **OpenFreeMap** | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf` | Used by the “liberty” style above. | | **MapTiler (free tier)** | `https://api.maptiler.com/tiles/v3/tiles.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Requires a free API key; good for production if you need a guaranteed SLA. | | **Stamen (raster)** | `https://stamen-tiles.a.ssl.fastly.net/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Raster only; you’d need a tiny style that references it. | | **Carto Positron (vector)** | `https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json` | Fully vector, no key. | > **Why the demo style is usually the fastest way to test:** > It already bundles everything (tiles, sprite, glyphs) on a CDN that’s CORS-enabled for browsers. You can focus on the *MapLibre* side of the migration (imports, namespace, token removal) without worrying about building a style yourself. --- ## 5️⃣ Checklist for “my map won’t load after removing the token” | ✅ | What to verify | |----|----------------| | **Package** – `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl` (or CDN change). | | **Import** – `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';` (or module CDN). | | **Namespace** – All `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl`. | | **Token** – Remove any `mapboxgl.accessToken = …` line. | | **Style URL** – Use a **non-`mapbox://`** URL (see the table above). | | **CORS** – The style JSON, sprite, glyphs, and tile endpoints must allow cross-origin requests (the public demo URLs do). | | **Console** – Open DevTools → Console → look for 404/403 errors that still reference `api.mapbox.com`. If you see them, you still have a stray Mapbox URL somewhere (e.g., in a custom source, sprite, or glyph URL). | | **Network** – Verify the style JSON loads (status 200) and that the tile requests (`*.pbf` or `*.png`) succeed. | If the console shows a 404 for the style URL, you’re still pointing at a `mapbox://…` URL. Replace it with one of the URLs above and the map should appear instantly. --- ## 6️⃣ Next steps after the test map works 1. **Choose a production tile source** – self-hosted PMTiles, Martin, TileServer-GL, or a paid provider (MapTiler, AWS, Azure). 2. **Create / edit your own style** – use **Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io) to edit the demo style or your exported style, then host the JSON. 3. **Swap in any Mapbox-specific plugins** – most UI plugins (NavigationControl, GeolocateControl, ScaleControl) work unchanged; for search/geocoding replace Mapbox Geocoder with **MapLibre-Geocoder**, **Pelias**, **Nominatim**, or **MapTiler Geocoding**. 4. **Performance tuning** – enable `preserveDrawingBuffer: false`, set `maxZoom`, `minZoom`, and consider using the **globe** projection (`projection: 'globe'`) if you need a world view. --- ### TL;DR Code snippet you can copy-paste ```js import * as maplibregl from 'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@^6.0.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs'; new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', // 👉 Use any of these three URLs: // style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json', // style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // style: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json', style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json', center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12 }).addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); ``` Drop that into a page, open it, and you’ll have a fully functional MapLibre map **without any API key**. From there you can start swapping in your own style or tile source. Happy mapping! 🚀

Description: anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre
prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including map.setFog() and some v2-specific camera features. After migrating to MapLibre, these are broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
You haven’t “broken” anything – you’re just running into the fact that **MapLibre GL JS never shipped the Mapbox-GL v2 APIs**. MapLibre was forked from **Mapbox GL JS v1.13** (December 2020) and has only added the features it needed under its own names. So calls such as `map.setFog()` or the free-camera helpers that exist in Mapbox GL v2 simply do not exist in MapLibre. Below is a quick-reference guide that explains why those calls fail, what the MapLibre equivalents are (or how to emulate them), and the extra migration steps you should double-check. --- ## 1️⃣ Why the calls are missing | Mapbox GL v2 feature | MapLibre status | What to do | |----------------------|----------------|------------| | `map.setFog({...})` | **Never implemented**. MapLibre uses a **`sky`** layer instead of a fog object. | Use `map.setSky()` (or `map.getSky()`) and add a `sky` entry to your style. | | `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` / `map.setFreeCameraOptions()` | **Never implemented**. MapLibre’s camera is expressed only via `center`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`, `elevation`, `roll`. | Compute a `CameraOptions` object with `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(...)` (or the older `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo`) and feed it to `jumpTo`, `easeTo`, or `flyTo`. | | `map.setTerrain({source: 'mapbox-dem', exaggeration: …})` (v2-only style syntax) | Supported, but the source must be a **non-Mapbox DEM** (e.g. a raster-DEM you host yourself or a third-party service). | Keep the call, just change the source definition. | | Any other `mapboxgl.*` v2-only methods (e.g. `setProjection('globe')` before v5) | Implemented in later MapLibre releases (v5+). | Verify you’re on a recent MapLibre version (≥ v5) and use the MapLibre name (`setProjection`, `setSky`, etc.). | --- ## 2️⃣ Re-implementing the fog → sky conversion ### 2.1 Add a `sky` entry to your style If you were using the default Mapbox “streets” style with fog, you can get a comparable look by adding a `sky` layer: ```json { "id": "sky", "type": "sky", "paint": { "sky-type": "atmosphere", "sky-color": "#199EF3", "sky-horizon-blend": 0.5, "sky-atmosphere-blend": 1, "sky-ground-blend": 0.5, "sky-fog-color": "#ffffff", "sky-fog-ground-blend": 0.3 } } ``` *Tip:* You can edit the style in **Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io) or directly in the JSON you load. ### 2.2 Call the runtime API (optional) If you need to change the sky dynamically: ```js // MapLibre (v5+) map.setSky({ 'sky-type': 'atmosphere', 'sky-color': '#199EF3', 'sky-horizon-blend': 0.5, 'sky-atmosphere-blend': 1, 'sky-ground-blend': 0.5, 'sky-fog-color': '#ffffff', 'sky-fog-ground-blend': 0.3 }); ``` > **Note:** The property names are the *style-spec* names (`sky-color`, `sky-fog-color`, …), **not** the old `fog` names. --- ## 3️⃣ Re-creating the free-camera behavior Mapbox’s free-camera API let you position the camera by a 3-D point (lng/lat/alt) and a rotation quaternion. In MapLibre you achieve the same result by: 1. **Calculate a `CameraOptions` object** from the desired 3-D pose. 2. **Pass that object** to `jumpTo`, `easeTo`, or `flyTo`. ```js // Example: look from 100 m above the ground, bearing 45°, pitch 60° const lng = -122.42; const lat = 37.78; const altitude = 100; // meters above the terrain const bearing = 45; // clockwise from north const pitch = 60; // degrees const roll = 0; // usually 0 // v5+ API – calculates the proper camera options const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( [lng, lat], // lng/lat altitude, // altitude in meters bearing, // bearing pitch, // pitch roll // roll ); // Move the camera instantly map.jumpTo(camOpts); // Or animate it map.easeTo({ ...camOpts, duration: 2000 }); ``` If you need a *look-at* (camera positioned at `from` and pointing at `to`), use the older helper (still available in v5): ```js const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromTo( [fromLng, fromLat], fromAltitude, [toLng, toLat], toAltitude, { bearing, pitch, roll } ); map.flyTo(camOpts); ``` ### 3.1 What you lose / gain | Feature | Mapbox v2 | MapLibre | |---------|-----------|----------| | Direct `FreeCameraOptions` class | ✅ | ❌ (replaced by `CameraOptions`) | | Built-in quaternion handling | ✅ | ❌ (you supply bearing/pitch/roll) | | Automatic terrain-aware altitude clamping | ✅ (via `setFog`) | ✅ (via `terrain` + `elevation` in `CameraOptions`) | | API stability | Proprietary, may change | Open-source, versioned, community-driven | --- ## 4️⃣ Quick sanity-check checklist (after you’ve already swapped the package, namespace, token, and style) | ✅ | Item | What to verify | |---|------|----------------| | 1 | **Package & import** | `npm i maplibre-gl@^6` (or the latest) and `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` (or `import {Map} from 'maplibre-gl'`). | | 2 | **Namespace** | All `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl`. Also CSS class prefixes (`mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`). | | 3 | **Access token** | No `maplibregl.accessToken` line. | | 4 | **Style URL** | Points to a non-Mapbox source (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` or your own style JSON). | | 5 | **Fog → Sky** | Either a `sky` layer in the style JSON **or** a runtime `map.setSky()` call. | | 6 | **Free-camera code** | Replaced with `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo`. | | 7 | **Terrain source** | If you still use `map.setTerrain`, the source must be a DEM you host or a third-party DEM (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/dem`). | | 8 | **Plugins** | Any Mapbox-only plugins (e.g. `mapbox-gl-geocoder`) swapped for MapLibre equivalents or open-source forks. | | 9 | **Geocoding / routing** | Replace Mapbox APIs with Nominatim, Photon, OSRM, OpenRouteService, etc., and update request URLs. | |10| **Test** | Open the page, verify the map loads, the sky appears, and the camera moves as expected. Check the browser console for “`map.setFog is not a function`” or similar errors – they should be gone. | If any of those items still show the old Mapbox code, you’ll see the same errors you reported. --- ## 5️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to fix them | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | `map.setFog is not a function` | Still calling `setFog` or using a style that contains a `fog` object. | Remove the call, add a `sky` layer, and/or call `map.setSky`. | | `map.getFreeCameraOptions is not a function` | Old free-camera code still present. | Replace with the `calculateCameraOptions…` flow described above. | | Map loads but tiles are 404 | Style still references `mapbox://` sources. | Edit the style JSON: change every source URL to a non-Mapbox endpoint (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/…`). | | Controls look broken | CSS class prefixes still `mapboxgl-`. | Update any custom CSS selectors to `maplibregl-`. | | `map.setProjection('globe')` throws | Using a MapLibre version < v5. | Upgrade to at least v5 (or v6) – globe projection was added in v5. | | Errors about missing `mapboxgl` global in a CDN script | You copied the old Mapbox CDN snippet. | Use the MapLibre module CDN snippet (see the migration guide) or bundle the ES-module version. | --- ## 6️⃣ Minimal working example (v6) ```html MapLibre – fog → sky demo
``` Run this in a modern browser (ES-module support required) and you should see: * a fully functional vector map, * a blue-sky background with a subtle horizon-fog effect, * an animated camera that lifts 200 m above the ground and tilts to 60° pitch. If this works, the migration core is solid; you can now re-integrate the rest of your app’s logic. --- ## 7️⃣ Where to go from here 1. **Validate your style** – `npx gl-style-validate style.json` (install `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`). 2. **Pick a tile source** – see the **maplibre-tile-sources** skill for self-hosted PMTiles, Martin, or third-party services. 3. **Replace Mapbox-only plugins** – e.g. `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` (fork) or a pure-JS geocoder that talks to Nominatim. 4. **Consider the new features** – MapLibre v6 adds WebGL2-only performance boosts, a Promise-based API, and the globe projection out-of-the-box. You may be able to simplify some of your code now. --- ### TL;DR *You didn’t miss a step; you’re simply trying to use Mapbox-v2 APIs that never existed in MapLibre.* Replace `setFog` with a `sky` layer (`map.setSky`), replace the free-camera helpers with `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo`, and make sure your style URL points to a non-Mapbox source. After those changes the rest of your map code should work unchanged. If you run into a specific error after applying the above, drop the exact console message and the snippet that triggers it – I can help troubleshoot the exact line. Happy mapping!

Description: implicit — finding compatible plugins after migration
prompt: I use several Mapbox GL JS plugins in my app and I'm migrating to MapLibre. How do I know which ones will still work?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **practical, step-by-step guide** you can use right after you have swapped the core library (Mapbox GL JS → MapLibre GL JS).  
It shows you how to **audit the plugins you already use**, decide which will keep working, and where to find a MapLibre-native replacement (or a small code change) for the ones that don’t.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick-scan checklist – “Does it still work out of the box?”

| ✅ Will work unchanged | ❓ Needs a check / small tweak | ❌ Will not work (Mapbox-only) |
|------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Pure UI helpers** that only touch the MapLibre API (e.g. `mapbox-gl-compare`, `mapbox-gl-rtl-text`, `mapbox-gl-language`, `mapbox-gl-zoom`, `mapbox-gl-fullscreen`, `mapbox-gl-geolocate`) | **Plugins that depend on Mapbox services** (e.g. `mapbox-gl-geocoder`, `mapbox-gl-directions`, `mapbox-gl-traffic`, `mapbox-gl-mapbox-tiles`) | **Plugins that import the Mapbox namespace directly** (`import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'`) **and never expose a way to inject a different `gl` object** (rare, but some older forks do this). |
| **Draw / edit tools** – `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` works because it only uses the core Map API. | **Style-related helpers** that read Mapbox-specific style properties (`mapbox-gl-style-switcher`, `mapbox-gl-legend` that expect a `mapbox://` sprite/glyph URL). | **Plugins that embed a Mapbox access-token request** (e.g. `mapbox-gl-heatmap` that pulls Mapbox-hosted tiles). |

> **Rule of thumb:** If the plugin **does not make any HTTP request to `api.mapbox.com` or `*.mapbox.com`**, it will most likely work unchanged.  
> If it **does** request Mapbox-hosted resources (tiles, sprites, glyphs, geocoding, directions, etc.) you’ll need to replace those services or swap the plugin for a MapLibre-native one.

---

## 2️⃣ How to verify each plugin

1. **Look at the repo / README**  
   * Search the repo for “MapLibre”, “maplibre-gl”, or “fork”.  
   * Many maintainers have already added a compatibility note (e.g. “Works with MapLibre GL JS ≥ 2.0”).

2. **Check `peerDependencies`** in `package.json`  
   ```json
   "peerDependencies": {
     "mapbox-gl": "^1.13.0 || ^2.0.0"
   }
   ```
   If the peer dep is **only** `mapbox-gl`, you can still install the plugin, but you must **alias** the import (see step 3). If the repo explicitly lists `maplibre-gl` as a peer, you’re good to go.

3. **Run a quick sanity test**  
   ```js
   import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';
   import MyPlugin from 'my-plugin';   // e.g. '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw'

   // If the plugin expects a global `mapboxgl` variable, give it one:
   window.mapboxgl = maplibregl;   // temporary shim for testing only

   const map = new maplibregl.Map({ … });
   const draw = new MyPlugin();    // or new MyPlugin.Draw()
   map.addControl(draw);
   ```
   *If the plugin throws “mapboxgl is not defined” or “cannot read property ‘Map’ of undefined”, you need a shim or a fork.*

4. **Watch the network tab**  
   * Look for any request to `*.mapbox.com` (tiles, sprites, glyphs, API endpoints).  
   * If you see them, you must replace the service (see section 4).

---

## 3️⃣ Shimming the old namespace (quick-fix only)

If a plugin hard-codes `import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'` **and** you cannot change the source, you can use an **npm alias** to make `mapbox-gl` resolve to `maplibre-gl`:

```bash
# npm v8+ or Yarn
npm install maplibre-gl@^6.0.0
npm install mapbox-gl@npm:maplibre-gl   # alias
```

or with **pnpm**:

```bash
pnpm add maplibre-gl@^6.0.0
pnpm add mapbox-gl@npm:maplibre-gl
```

> **Caution:** This works for most plugins that only use the core API, but it **does not** magically replace Mapbox-hosted URLs. You’ll still have to point the map’s `style`, `sprite`, `glyphs`, and any source URLs to non-Mapbox endpoints.

---

## 4️⃣ Replacing Mapbox-only services

| Mapbox service used by plugin | Typical plugin | MapLibre-compatible alternative | What you need to change |
|-------------------------------|----------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Geocoding / search** | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` | `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` (fork) or custom UI that calls Nominatim / Pelias / MapTiler Geocoding | Update the endpoint URL and token handling. |
| **Directions / routing** | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions` | `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions` (community fork) or roll your own with OSRM / OpenRouteService | Change the request URL and response parsing if needed. |
| **Traffic tiles** | `mapbox-gl-traffic` | Use a traffic vector source from a provider (e.g. OpenTraffic, TomTom, MapTiler) and style it yourself | Replace the source URL (`mapbox://mapbox.mapbox-traffic-v1`) with your own source. |
| **Mapbox Tiles / Sprites / Glyphs** | Any plugin that loads a `mapbox://` style or sprite | Host your own style JSON, sprite PNG/JSON, and glyph PBF (or use a public style like OpenFreeMap) | Change the `style` URL, `sprite` and `glyphs` fields in the style JSON. |
| **Mapbox Satellite / Terrain** | `mapbox-gl-compare` (when comparing a Mapbox satellite style) | Use a free satellite source (e.g. `https://tiles.stadiamaps.com/tiles/alidade_satellite/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`) or a self-hosted raster source | Update the source definition in your style. |
| **Mapbox Terrain RGB** | `mapbox-gl-terrain` (adds terrain source) | `maplibre-gl-terrain` (same API, just a different package name) | Install `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-terrain` and point the source URL to a non-Mapbox terrain provider (e.g. `https://tiles.stadiamaps.com/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`). |

> **Tip:** The **awesome-maplibre** repo (https://github.com/maplibre/awesome-maplibre) maintains a curated list of plugins that already ship a MapLibre-compatible version. Start there before you decide to fork a plugin yourself.

---

## 5️⃣ Popular Mapbox GL JS plugins → MapLibre equivalents (or “works as-is”)

| Mapbox plugin | MapLibre status | Recommended replacement / notes |
|---------------|----------------|---------------------------------|
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` | ✅ Works unchanged (only core API) | Keep using it. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` | ✅ Fork exists: `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` | Install the fork; same API. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions` | ✅ Fork exists: `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions` | Same API, just change import. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-compare` | ✅ Works unchanged (UI only) | Keep, but replace any Mapbox style URLs you compare against. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-traffic` | ❓ Depends on Mapbox traffic source | Replace source with a third-party traffic vector source or drop the plugin. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-heatmap` | ✅ Works (heatmap is a style layer) | Keep; just ensure your style uses a non-Mapbox source. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-language` | ✅ Works (adds language support) | Keep; just change the `style` source. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-rtl-text` | ✅ Works (text shaping) | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-legend` | ❓ May reference Mapbox sprite URLs | Fork and replace `sprite` URL, or use `maplibre-gl-legend` (community fork). |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-zoom` | ✅ Works (simple UI control) | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-fullscreen` | ✅ Works | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geolocate` | ✅ Works | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-scale` | ✅ Works | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-rotate` | ✅ Works | Keep. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-heatmap-layer` (third-party) | ✅ Usually works | Verify it doesn’t request Mapbox tiles. |
| `mapbox-gl-js` **extensions** (e.g. `mapbox-gl-animate`, `mapbox-gl-curve`) | ❓ Depends on internal Mapbox APIs | Test; most will work because they only use the public Map API. |

---

## 6️⃣ When you need to **fork or patch** a plugin

1. **Clone the repo** and change the import:
   ```diff
   - import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl';
   + import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';
   ```
2. **Update any hard-coded URLs** (`mapbox://` → your source).  
   If the plugin builds a style object internally, replace the `source` definition with a generic `vector` source that points to your own tiles.

3. **Publish a scoped fork** (e.g. `@myorg/mapbox-gl-draw-maplibre`) or open a PR on the original repo. Many plugin maintainers are happy to add a `maplibre` entry to `peerDependencies`.

4. **Add a small shim** for the old namespace (only for development):
   ```js
   // src/shim.js – load before any plugin
   import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';
   window.mapboxgl = maplibregl;   // makes old plugins think they have mapboxgl
   ```

   **Do not ship this shim in production** unless you are certain the plugin never reaches out to Mapbox services.

---

## 7️⃣ Testing checklist after you’ve swapped plugins

| ✅ Test | What to verify |
|--------|----------------|
| **Map loads** | No `Failed to load style` errors; all sprite/glyph URLs resolve (check Network tab). |
| **Controls appear** | All UI controls (navigation, geolocate, fullscreen, draw, etc.) render and respond. |
| **Plugin UI works** | Open the plugin UI (e.g., geocoder dropdown, directions panel) and confirm it shows results. |
| **Network traffic** | No requests to `*.mapbox.com` unless you deliberately use a Mapbox-hosted service (which you probably don’t). |
| **Feature interaction** | Click/drag events, drawing, editing, route drawing, heatmap updates, etc., all behave as before. |
| **Performance** | No console warnings about deprecated Mapbox APIs; frame-rate comparable to before. |
| **Build size** | Verify that the bundle no longer includes the large Mapbox GL source (run `webpack-bundle-analyzer` or similar). |

---

## 8️⃣ Quick “one-liner” cheat sheet for the most common plugins

```bash
# Core migration
npm uninstall mapbox-gl
npm install maplibre-gl@^6

# Plugins that work unchanged
npm i @mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw @mapbox/mapbox-gl-language @mapbox/mapbox-gl
